dedupe_keys.name: copernicus global human settlement layer ghsl built up surface and population grids

description: The Global Human Settlement Layer produces global spatial information, evidence-based analytics and knowledge describing the human presence on the planet, using automated processing of global fine-scale satellite image streams, census data and crowdsourced or volunteered geographic information. The JRC, with the European Commission's directorates-general for regional and urban policy and for defence industry and space, is working towards regular operational monitoring of global built-up areas and population from Sentinel observations. The Humanitarian Data Exchange entry, published by Copernicus, provides GHS built-up surface and GHS population grids as downloadable GeoTIFF files under CC BY, citing the R2023A multitemporal releases for 1975 to 2030 (built-up surface from Sentinel-2 and Landsat composites; population grid by Schiavina and co-authors), with country subsets such as India and Iran also queued. Caveats: the multitemporal series extends to 2030, beyond observed dates, and HDX holds selected layers while the full product family is on the JRC and Copernicus sites. It is a standard exposure layer for hazard exposure analysis, emergency response and capacity planning of infrastructure serving settlements, and for climate adaptation screening; a related record is the Meta high resolution population density maps.
name: Copernicus Global Human Settlement Layer (GHSL) built-up surface and population grids
notes: One record covers the global GHSL entry and the India and Iran subsets on HDX. JRC data pages are behind a WAF from the cloud browser; facts are from the HDX entry.
